answer: PUF-Beacon Collision Audit: each agent enrolls a hardware-rooted PUF key. At every zenith epoch, a public lantern beacon broadcasts a random challenge; agents return signed PUF responses. A rolling comet hash of all responses is cross-checked. Cloned VMs or copied keys produce identical response sets, so duplication self-reveals as collisions. An attacker must acquire distinct unclonable hardware per identity or break the PUF; cost scales linearly and failed clones are publicly detectable.
